prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1185; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve. Both drivers reported at scene. Initial liability appears disputed pending statements. Assigned to field adjuster for vehicle inspection.

Entry 2: Vehicle inspection completed. Front bumper, hood, and both headlamp assemblies show damage consistent with low-speed impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop. Photos uploaded to file.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. Letter of representation received. All further contact to go through attorney's office. Claimant reports neck and upper back pain with onset the day after the accident. Medical records and treatment authorization requested through counsel. Diagnosis on file is whiplash.

Entry 4: Recorded statement taken from insured. Consistent with first notice account. Insured states speed was under 25 miles per hour and reports no prior claims for neck or back complaints. Witness contact information obtained from police report and outreach letter sent.

Entry 5: Demand package received from claimant's attorney, including treatment summary and medical bills. Reviewing treatment notes for consistency with reported injury and timeline. Referred to bodily injury unit for evaluation. Reserves reviewed and adjusted. Next follow-up set for review of records and response to counsel.
